families.axis: bare standing that could go either way → being held in high esteem and honor

members.gloss: good repute
members.tone: The good is built into the word here, so unlike *name* it needs no adjective to come out favorable.

members.gloss: a person's reputation
members.tone: The plainest term for what a person is held to be, carrying no verdict of its own and taking whatever *character* or disgrace is attached to it.

members.gloss: the reputation and popularity a person has
members.tone: Treats standing as a quantity that rises and falls, and pairs it with popularity rather than the honor *reputation* names.

members.gloss: the state of being held in high esteem and honor
members.tone: The full weight of the family: not merely being thought well of but being held in high esteem and honor.

members.gloss: favorable public reputation
members.tone: Adds breadth to approval — the favor is public, where *character* keeps good standing a private matter.

members.gloss: the state of being held in high esteem and honor
members.tone: The formal counterpart to *reputation*, stating the same high esteem and honor in a more elevated register.

families.axis: a standing source of help and counsel → a rescuer from actual danger

members.gloss: a source of help and advice and encouragement
members.tone: Warm and informal, casting the helper as a standing resource of help, advice and encouragement rather than a one-off saviour like *deliverer*.

members.gloss: someone who supports or champions something
members.tone: Approving, but aimed at a thing supported or championed rather than at a person in trouble, so the credit is for backing and advocacy rather than for relief.

members.gloss: a person who rescues you from harm or danger
members.tone: The most elevated of the three and the most urgent, since the help it names is rescue from harm or danger, not the encouragement of *uncle*.

families.axis: self-esteem swollen past reason → that swollen self-esteem turned outward as a superior manner toward those below

members.gloss: unreasonable and inordinate self-esteem (personified as one of the deadly sins)
members.tone: Here the word is a vice and not a virtue - self-esteem grown unreasonable and past all proportion, and grave enough to stand as one of the deadly sins.

members.gloss: overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors
members.tone: A flat accusation: the swollen self-regard of *pride* has stopped being inward and is now overbearing, worn as a superior manner toward those it counts as inferior.

members.gloss: overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors
members.tone: Formal and chilly, naming the same overbearing pride as a bearing one carries above inferiors rather than levelling the blunt charge *arrogance* makes.

families.axis: a face kept up to impress → a deliberate, overdone pose

members.gloss: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
members.tone: The mildest word here for faking it, faulting the wish to look good rather than the falsehood itself, which is where *pretence* puts the blame.

members.gloss: pretending that something is the case in order to make a good impression
members.tone: Treats the same impression-making pretence as something staged for onlookers, with more of a sneer at the performance than *appearance* carries.

members.gloss: a deliberate pretense or exaggerated display
members.tone: Convicts the pretence of being both calculated and laid on too thick, so the fault is excess as much as falsity.

members.gloss: the act of giving a false appearance
members.tone: The flat, general name for putting up a false front, with none of the flattering motive that softens *appearance* and no charge of overdoing it; British spelling.

families.axis: an outcome loosely held in mind → a fixed point aimed at that ends the effort

members.gloss: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
members.tone: The weightiest of the plain words for a wanted outcome: it frames that outcome as what gives the planned action its reason, where *aim* only gives it a direction.

members.gloss: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
members.tone: Puts the anticipated outcome in the mind of whoever is acting, so it holds whether or not anything is done about it, unlike *target* with its attainable thing to be hit.

members.gloss: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
members.tone: Makes the intended outcome sound worked out in advance, a shape already settled on rather than the bare wish *intention* names.

members.gloss: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
members.tone: Clipped and formal beside *intention*, stating the outcome as something fixed on rather than merely entertained.

members.gloss: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions
members.tone: The lightest and most directional of these: it points at the outcome without the justifying weight *purpose* carries.

members.gloss: the state of affairs that a plan is intended to achieve and that (when achieved) terminates behavior intended to achieve it
members.tone: Abstract and cool, naming the outcome as the terminus at which the behaviour stops, where *goal* names the same thing as something worked toward.

members.gloss: the goal intended to be attained (and which is believed to be attainable)
members.tone: Dry and formal, presenting the wanted outcome as a definite thing to be got and believed gettable, without *target*'s invitation to score a hit or a miss.

members.gloss: the state of affairs that a plan is intended to achieve and that (when achieved) terminates behavior intended to achieve it
members.tone: The plainest everyday word for the achievement a plan runs to and stops at, warmer and less abstract than *end* for the same thing.

members.gloss: the ultimate goal for which something is done
members.tone: Sets the outcome as the ultimate one, the point everything else is serving, and carries the figure of a journey's end that *object* does not.

members.gloss: the goal intended to be attained (and which is believed to be attainable)
members.tone: The sharpest of these: it makes the attainable outcome a thing to be struck, so falling short of it registers as a miss.

families.axis: bare giving of evidence → taking on the role of informer

members.gloss: act as an informer
members.tone: Casts the act as a role rather than an occasion — you are not someone who spoke but an informer, and the faint taint sits in that role where *tell* has none.

members.gloss: give evidence
members.tone: The plainest verb available for producing evidence, naming the act and implying nothing about the one who does it.

families.axis: nastiness of temper → a quality that threatens evil

members.gloss: malevolence by virtue of being malicious or spiteful or nasty
members.tone: Malevolence run down to nastiness — it takes in the merely nasty as readily as the truly malicious, so it can bite without carrying the threat *malice* carries.

members.gloss: the quality of threatening evil
members.tone: The heaviest word here: not an unpleasant streak but a quality that holds evil over someone.

members.gloss: the quality of being cruel and causing tension or annoyance
members.tone: Names the cruel disposition itself, but pitched at the tension and annoyance it inflicts rather than at any graver damage.

members.gloss: the quality of being deliberately mean
members.tone: Deliberateness is the whole of the charge — not a lapse or a bad mood but meanness meant, which is what condemns it.

families.axis: a single act of disrespect → conduct condemned as morally evil

members.gloss: morally objectionable behavior
members.tone: The flat, absolute name for conduct that offends morality, condemning without argument or degree.

members.gloss: morally objectionable behavior
members.tone: Condemns the same conduct with a moralizing relish, as though the wrong were knowingly savoured rather than merely done — fuller-blooded than the bare *evil*.

members.gloss: a disrespectful act
members.tone: Frames the disrespect as a breach, something owed and transgressed, giving the act a hard formal weight that *irreverence* lacks.

members.gloss: a disrespectful act
members.tone: The lightest blame here: an act that withholds due respect rather than one that breaks anything.
